book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Bush with, 'Are we to shift position?'

indicators.note: to shift is to move things about, so the letters of the four words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former president asks his team whether it is time to change their stance on an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the American president or a shrub, but it is just four letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's whereabouts is the place where they are, their location.

clue.text: Bone of old king seen in soil

indicators.note: the king's letters are found inside the soil word

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, the title of a former King Edward

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch's skeleton is discovered buried in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm, between shoulder and elbow.

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something new, so the letters change into another word

explanation.surface: Something lies motionless before suddenly floating.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient, like buoyant, describes someone who bounces back cheerfully after setbacks.

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so the drug's letter is lost

explanation.surface: American states turn against the use of a party drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like a noun for countries or US states; it is the verb meaning declares.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare or assert firmly, so avers means asserts.

indicators.note: the preaching word goes about, or around, the exercise letters

parts.note: to orate is to speak like a preacher, at length

explanation.surface: A fitness fanatic jogs and lectures everyone on keeping fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like jogging, but the definition is in the sense of running a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a business or machine is to run it, control it and keep it working.

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the phrase is replaced by a near-identical sounding word

parts.note: trusted means believed in on faith

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be held by religious belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound by faith' reads as one phrase about devotion, but 'Bound' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means tied up tightly, as a chicken is before roasting.

clue.text: New dawn from Iran as scene changes

indicators.note: something that changes takes a different shape, so the letters of the scene are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh start comes to Iran as its political landscape shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A renaissance is a rebirth or revival, a fresh beginning after a dark period.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the caped crime-fighter of Gotham City himself; the 's stands for 'is'
second meaning: an army officer's personal servant, always at his side

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to ask for the superhero's young companion; instead the superhero is the answer, and his name is also the word for an officer's attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A batman is a soldier who serves as a British army officer's personal servant, while Batman is the comic-book crime-fighter.

clue.text: Luther, as muse, contains his opponent

indicators.note: the phrase before it holds the answer's letters running across its words

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of Luther, through as, into muse

explanation.surface: The reformer Martin Luther, acting as someone's inspiration, harbours his own rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's own subject: the humanist scholar Erasmus clashed with Luther over free will.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch humanist Erasmus wrote against Luther's views on free will, making him Luther's famous intellectual adversary.

clue.text: Fantastic view from French tower, we hear

indicators.note: what is heard is a spoken sound, so the tower's name stands for a word that sounds like it

explanation.surface: A tourist describes the marvellous panorama from the top of the Paris landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is a striking or remarkable sight, something well worth looking at.

clue.text: Certain I'm in trouble getting blame

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in a mess, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A worried suspect is sure they will be held responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: To incriminate is to accuse someone or make them appear guilty of a fault.

definitions.meaning: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea, not 'the principal'
the person in charge there: the naval officer who commands a fleet

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main man' reads as slang for the most important person; read 'main' as the sea and the man who rules it is a top naval officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the highest rank of naval officer, the commander of a fleet at sea.

clue.text: Unfinished final performance for film star

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its last part, so the closing letter is cut

parts.note: a swan song is an artist's last appearance

explanation.surface: An actor's farewell appearance is cut short before the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood silent-era actress, best remembered for Sunset Boulevard.

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: only its first letter is used
ends are leftover scraps, as in odds and ends

explanation.surface: A national leader tears up official messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of state' looks like a president or monarch; it is just the first letter of 'state'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch something is to send it off, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Cockney man's caring for the audience

indicators.note: words spoken for listeners are heard rather than read, so the phrase is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: the man is HE, so this is 'he's tender' (tender meaning caring), said as a Cockney would with the H dropped

explanation.surface: A Londoner describes a kind fellow while talking to a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop their H, so 'he's tender' comes out as 'e's tender, which sounds like the answer; 'Cockney' does double duty as definition and as the hint to drop the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockneys come from London's East End, so an East Ender is a native Cockney.

indicators.note: a false arrangement is not the genuine one, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone shields a lying person who gives evidence in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False witness' reads as a perjurer; split it, and 'false' works on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker who watches an event, as a witness sees what happens.

indicators.note: deconstruction takes a text apart, so the letters of the three words before it are taken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A thinker is wide awake to the fashionable critical theory of taking texts apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato and tutor of Alexander the Great.

indicators.note: the example abbreviation sits inside the word for between

parts.note: inter- is the Latin prefix meaning between

explanation.surface: Someone, say, is caught in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: One is a whole number, the simplest example of a positive integer.

clue.text: Thanks to hospital, gripped by depression

indicators.note: the hospital letter is held inside the depression word

parts.note: a trough is a low area or hollow

explanation.surface: Someone is grateful to a hospital while held in the grip of depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thanks' looks like gratitude to the hospital; 'Thanks to' together is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Through can mean by means of or because of, as in 'succeeded through hard work'.

parts.note: to ream is to widen or bore out a hole

explanation.surface: A dull Tory politician offers voters an option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person, but here it is the verb for drilling out a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, the pick or choice of the bunch.

parts.note: mist is a fine spray of liquid

explanation.surface: A device that squirts out a rebellious kind of spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispenser' suggests an aerosol; it is a person who makes up and hands out medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a chemist is a pharmacist, the person who dispenses prescription drugs.

indicators.note: the petition word sits inside the final word

parts.note: the end is the final part
to sue is to petition or appeal formally

explanation.surface: Something led to a last appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means followed as a consequence, so it came about as a result.

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Lake Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A rowing team ends up on the bottom of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' looks like a boat's rowers and 'bed' like a lake bottom; instead the bed is a small bed sitting on top of a lake's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group of people, a crowd or set, as a crew can be.

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to live is to pass one's time or days

explanation.surface: Skipping the day of rest exposes a person's wrongdoings.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the dictionary abbreviation for Sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: Evils are wicked acts or wrongdoings, the moral wrongs that sins are.

clue.text: Tory leader has grounds for disaffection

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter, so only the first of 'Tory' is taken

parts.note: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party
grounds for an action are the reason for it

explanation.surface: The Conservative chief has cause to feel alienated from his party.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the most extreme form of political disloyalty.

clue.text: A disease found by one rodent

parts.note: gout is a disease that inflames the joints
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An illness is discovered next to a single rat or mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a long-legged South American rodent related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Most banal time on divinity exam

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, an old school name for the subject

explanation.surface: A scripture paper set on the clock was the dullest test ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite means hackneyed and overused, so the superlative is the most hackneyed.

clue.text: Arrange putting value on gold coffer

indicators.note: putting one thing on another sets it after it here, so the value word follows the gold and coffer words

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest
to rate something is to put a value on it

explanation.surface: Someone sets about pricing a treasure box made of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting value on gold coffer' places the value word after the other two in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate is to organise or coordinate something carefully, like music for an orchestra.
